          CARE HEROES

          People who bring healthcare closer to the village

          GramCare is designed around teamwork. Doctors provide clinical review, ASHA/community workers help families use care services, and ambulance teams support safe emergency transport and hospital coordination.

          Doctor support

          Doctors review, guide and follow up

          Doctors can review recorded observations, understand patient history, conduct teleconsultations and decide when an in-person examination or escalation is needed.

          • Reviews measurements and symptoms shared by authorized workers.
          • Provides professional consultation and follow-up planning.
          • Receives pre-arrival information during a simulated emergency transfer.
          ASHA / Community care

          A trusted bridge between villagers and doctors

          Community health workers can help people with limited digital literacy record observations, find care, schedule follow-ups and use offline workflows when connectivity is weak.

          • Assists with basic digital health recording.
          • Supports reminders, referrals and doctor connections.
          • Can initiate the demo emergency workflow when authorized.
          Ambulance & rescue

          Emergency transport with better coordination

          The ambulance module demonstrates assignment, ETA, live location updates and hospital pre-arrival information so the care team can follow one coordinated emergency journey.

          • Shows a reviewable ambulance recommendation and assignment.
          • Shares simulated location, status and ETA.
          • Supports simulated transport-vital updates to the receiving facility.

          Photos and scenarios on this prototype illustrate healthcare roles. Emergency dispatch, availability and medical readings shown in the demo are not live services.

          GRAMCARE BLOG

          Simple health-tech information for rural care

          Short educational articles explaining how the platform is intended to help communities. These articles provide general information, not medical diagnosis or treatment advice.

          Offline care · 4 min read

          Why offline-first healthcare matters in villages

          When mobile data drops, essential observations should not simply disappear. GramCare demonstrates saving records on the device first and synchronizing them when connectivity returns.

          Try offline monitoring →
          Remote care · 5 min read

          How remote monitoring can support doctor review

          Recorded heart rate, SpO₂, temperature and blood pressure can help organize a review workflow, while clinical interpretation remains with qualified healthcare professionals.

          View monitoring demo →
          Emergency coordination · 4 min read

          From SOS to hospital: reducing information gaps

          A coordinated emergency flow can connect the patient location, responder status, ambulance ETA and receiving facility so authorized teams have a clearer shared picture.

          See alert & tracking →
          Community care · 3 min read

          Why follow-up is as important as the first consultation

          Reminders and community-worker visits can help patients remember appointments, measurements and planned reviews after a consultation or hospital visit.

          Explore patient records →

          Why it matters

          📶

          Patchy connectivity breaks most digital health tools — GramCare stores first, syncs later.

          ⏱️

          Distance delays emergency care — transparent dispatch recommendations save minutes, with humans deciding.

          🗣️

          Language and literacy gaps — Hindi/English, large text, icons and voice help.

          🔒

          Privacy by design — role-based access, consent and audit logs in the full stack.

          Full stack plan: Java Spring Boot API · C edge engine · MySQL · simulators. This page is the front-end demo.
